scope: targeted CPU crop and 16-bit export regressions
exclusions: shader/native GPU edits or hardware tests
fix: Pass the existing compatibility flag into private glass_unmasked; keep its original RGBA8 quantization only for legacy SDR and retain extended-linear floating-point RGB/alpha for explicitly color-managed documents. No sampling, distance-field, blur, refraction, lighting or tolerance changes.

checks.phase: final formatted implementation and added finite-range boundary

newTestCoverage.assertion: Whole-frame exact Pixel equality with effect disabled; both managed profiles, alpha 0, 1/4096, 1/4, 1/2, 1 and an opaque +/-65504 finite-range boundary. No relaxed tolerance.
Nonzero blur, refraction and light retain exact constant interior, HDR/negative edge channels and finite bounded alpha in both profiles.
Exact floating-point crop-vs-1024-wide tiled frame equality across the 512 boundary at 1x/2x/3x, with translucent HDR gradient, fractional rounded geometry and ancestor clip.
Both profiles at 1x/2x/3x retain exact PQ PNG bytes compared with disabled zero-distortion effect; decoded metadata is 16-bit with expected dimensions.
SHA-256 of full CPU RGBA output matches pre-change 077d111 for analytic, figma and figmaSubpixel, using translucent gradient and nonzero glass parameters.

coverageLimits: Five Rust test functions exercise 29 parameter configurations; this is not 29 separate test-runner cases.
Tiled crop cases use nonzero blur but zero refraction/light. They do not prove tile invariance for arbitrary refractive displacement.
The nonzero-refraction fixture uses a constant backdrop and tests range/alpha, not displacement direction or amplitude.
SDR hashes come from the unmodified CPU implementation, not independent Figma exports.
A 1/255 channel-value difference is not a 1px geometric displacement.
Portable kernel tests include CPU-side GPU packet/compiler contracts; no native GPU crate or hardware renderer was built or executed.
These passing CPU checks do not establish whole-product production readiness or full Figma parity.
